repository_card.frontier: Finite-sample validity and repaired dual witnesses are distinct from statistical power and global hierarchy completeness.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: The HNW lower bounds offer a model-boundary audit for proposed universal SDP extensions. Dictionary: common feasible region -> one relaxation serving every measurement. The existing fixed-observable localizer need not satisfy that universal model.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Record dimension, accuracy, observable family and whether the feasible region is shared. Run the existing exact witness verifier, then design a visibility-negative-control experiment with an unobserved slow mode.
repository_card.falsifier: Abandon a universal-completeness claim if it requires a fixed SDP size in a dimension/accuracy regime excluded by HNW. Do not infer such a lower bound for a single scalar moment instance.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Semidefinite extension complexity of the separable set, with applications to approximate disentanglers
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: introduction, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, Section 3 and formalization links
sources.source_claim: Gharibian, Hecht and Rudolph give dimension- and accuracy-dependent lower bounds for semidefinite representations of separable-state optimization in the HNW model. The paper links a companion Lean development.
sources.limits: The common feasible region and objective-independent embedding are essential. This is not a lower bound for every SDP or for unrestricted SAT circuits. The paper credits a stronger concurrent disentangler result to Bostanci et al.; its SDP result has a distinct scope. External Lean proofs were not rebuilt here.

sources.title: A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Bostanci and collaborators report a quantum-oracle separation of QMA(2) from QMA and derive exponential input-size requirements for approximate disentanglers with total error below one.
sources.limits: Oracle separation is not an unrelativized class separation. Universal coverage of separable states is much stronger than recovery of one reference state or a restricted code. First posted 2 September.

sources.title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Anshu and collaborators construct constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expanders with depth-one local circuit realizations and apply them to one-dimensional Hamiltonians with an entanglement-gap relation.
sources.limits: An expander gap, a transfer gap and a many-body Hamiltonian gap are different operators. Track dimension, locality and the definition of gap before translating. First posted 1 September.
